meta_description: Family-owned, City-licensed electricians for Wicker Park Victorians, two- and three-flats and new builds, about 35 permits here since 2012. Call (773) 262-3333.
eyebrow: Wicker Park · Milwaukee Avenue · Division Street · The 606
hero_lede: Panel and service upgrades, rewiring, lighting, EV chargers, repairs and new-construction wiring, for Wicker Park's Victorian houses, brick two- and three-flats, new three-unit buildings and the storefronts on Milwaukee, Division and North Ave. Family-owned and founder-led, licensed by the City of Chicago, and working these blocks since 2012, with every quote in writing.
boundary_text: The City's neighbourhood map draws Wicker Park from the 606 trail (Bloomingdale Ave) south to Division Street, and from Ashland Avenue west to Rockwell Street, just past Western Avenue; many people put the northern edge at North Avenue. It's a neighbourhood of 1870s to 1920s houses and flats around a small park, cut through diagonally by the Milwaukee Avenue shopping street.

districts.name: Wicker Park District
districts.intro: The City landmark district around the park itself, from Potomac Ave up to Caton St and from Bell Ave east to the 'L': houses built from 1870 to 1930, with some of Chicago's largest Victorians on Pierce Ave and on Hoyne Ave, once called Beer Baron Row.
districts.work: Whole-house work in big old houses: 200-amp services, new panels and rewiring behind plaster. Exterior changes go through landmark permit review.

districts.name: Milwaukee Avenue
districts.intro: The diagonal shopping street from Division and Ashland up to North and Damen, a City landmark district of storefront buildings from 1870 to 1929, including the Art Deco Northwest Tower at Damen and North, plus the side streets east of Damen: Wood, Wolcott, Paulina and Honore.
districts.work: Shop, salon, bar and restaurant fit-outs, storefront signs and the flats above the shops. On the side streets, renovations and new three-unit buildings.

districts.name: Division Street
districts.intro: Bars, restaurants, shops and daycares along Division from Ashland to Rockwell, with brick flats on the blocks just north.
districts.work: Restaurant and shop work, build-outs in ground-floor commercial spaces, and repairs and new lighting in the flats above.

districts.name: Toward Western and Rockwell
districts.intro: The blocks of Oakley, Claremont, Artesian and Campbell west of the landmark district, where older brick two- and three-flats sit next to new houses and three-unit buildings.
districts.work: Wiring for new houses and three-flats, 100-to-200-amp service upgrades with new meters, and EV chargers in garages off the alleys.

districts.name: North Ave to the 606
districts.intro: The strip between North Ave and the elevated 606 trail, around Wabansia Ave, Wood St, Hoyne Ave and Artesian Ave.
districts.work: New houses with detached garages, kitchen circuits and recessed lighting in renovated houses, and service upgrades.

scope_lede: The same job on paper can cost very differently in a Victorian on Hoyne, a brick three-flat on Oakley and a storefront on Milwaukee. These are the things that change it, and most are settled at the walkthrough.
scope_rows: In the Wicker Park District and the Milwaukee Avenue District, the Commission on Chicago Landmarks reviews alterations to buildings, so exterior electrical work such as a service mast, a meter move, exterior lighting or a sign can need its sign-off before the permit is issued.
Houses and flats built between the 1870s and the 1920s can still hide knob-and-tube, cloth-covered cable or a fuse box behind later remodels.
Two- and three-flats often still share a 100-amp service. Our upgrades on N Oakley Blvd moved buildings to 200 amps with three or four new meters and panels.
Fishing wire through plaster is slower than drywall, and openings are kept small so patching stays small.
Turning a three-flat back into one house, or digging out a basement, means a new service and every circuit redesigned from the architect's plans.
You and us, with your architect
Power for a garage or an EV charger means a feed from the house, sometimes underground, sized for what you'll run.
A new business sign needs its own sign permit, separate from the electrical permit.
In flats that are now condos, the association approves work in the basement, on the meters and in common areas, usually from a written proposal.
Parking near the door is scarce on Milwaukee, Division and North Ave, so on many jobs materials come in from the alley.
Stand-alone electrical jobs usually go through the City's Express Permit Program. New buildings, renovations and build-outs need plans and a full permit.
Bars, restaurants, shops and daycares often need work before opening or after closing, so agree the hours before the job is scheduled.
hourly_answer: We quote by scope, not by the hour, because the hours on a Wicker Park job depend on the factors below. A new circuit in a gutted three-flat on Campbell and the same circuit fished through the plaster of a Victorian on Hoyne aren't the same job. The written quote tells you the whole price before you agree to it.
choosing_building_why: A Victorian in a landmark district, a three-flat on a 100-amp service and a storefront with flats upstairs are three different jobs.
choosing_building_answer: In Wicker Park: new houses and three-unit buildings west and east of Damen, 200-amp service upgrades with new meters on N Oakley Blvd, a three-to-one de-conversion on N Hoyne, and daycare build-outs on W Division and W North Ave
choosing_paperwork_why: Exterior work in the Wicker Park and Milwaukee Avenue landmark districts goes through landmark review, and storefront signs need their own permit.
where_we_fit: Highlights is a family-owned contractor. In Wicker Park we're the right call for Victorian houses, two- and three-flats, de-conversions, new houses and three-unit buildings, service upgrades, EV chargers in alley garages, and fit-outs for shops, daycares and restaurants. Large apartment developments and big commercial projects are a job for the large commercial firms, and we'll tell you so.

honest_context: Wicker Park sits in the middle of our work. Most of our roughly 1,200 Chicago permits are in Wards 1, 32, 26, 47 and 27, and the first three of those are the wards that split Wicker Park. Our permits here, about 35, run from 2012 to 2025, with the busiest years from 2013 to 2018, when we wired new houses and three-unit buildings. Since then the work has been more mixed: service upgrades, renovations, a few new buildings and commercial spaces.

Wicker Park is a busy permit area: about 410 permits with electrical work in the last 24 months, naming about 190 different electrical contractors. Most of it is the work we do every day, in units, lighting and services. Signs are a large share too, from the storefronts on the shopping streets; we hold one sign permit here, on N Milwaukee.

faq: Does the Wicker Park landmark district change electrical work?

It can, if the work changes the outside. The Wicker Park District, around the park from Potomac Ave to Caton St, and the Milwaukee Avenue District are City landmark districts, and the Commission on Chicago Landmarks reviews alterations there as part of the permit. A new service mast, a moved meter, exterior lighting or a sign can need its sign-off, and we check at the walkthrough whether yours does.
Can you upgrade the service in my Wicker Park two- or three-flat?

Yes. Our Wicker Park record includes two buildings on N Oakley Blvd moved from 100-amp to 200-amp services, with three and four new meters and panels. We pull the permit, usually through the City's Express Permit Program, and work with ComEd on the service change.
Do you wire de-conversions and gut rehabs?

Yes. On the 1200 block of N Hoyne we did the electrical for a three-unit building turned back into one house with a two-storey addition, and on the 1300 block of N Wolcott an interior remodel of a four-unit building with a basement dig-down. These run under a permit with plans, and we work from your architect's drawings.
Do you do the electrical for new houses and three-flats in Wicker Park?

Yes. Half our Wicker Park permits, 17 of 34, are new construction: houses with detached garages on N Campbell, N Artesian, N Wood and N Marion Ct, buildings of two to six units on N Paulina, N Claremont, N Artesian, N Campbell, N Wood and N Honore, and a four-storey mixed-use building on W North Ave.
Can you work on a storefront on Milwaukee Ave, Division St or North Ave?

Yes: build-outs, lighting, signs and service work, scheduled around your hours. Our record includes daycare build-outs on W Division and W North Ave, and a tenant space and its sign on N Milwaukee. A new sign needs its own sign permit, and on Milwaukee Ave it can also need landmark review.
Which Wicker Park ZIP codes do you cover?
Both: 60622, which covers most of Wicker Park, and 60647, which covers the blocks north of North Ave and west of Damen. We cover every other Chicago neighbourhood too.
